claim: The mature cerebellum controls motor skill precision and participates in other sophisticated brain functions that include learning, cognition, and speech.
source: The mature cerebellum controls motor skill precision and participates in other sophisticated brain functions that include learning, cognition, and speech.
evidence: This is a general statement about cerebellar function that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Different types of GABAergic and glutamatergic cerebellar neurons originate in temporal order from two progenitor niches, the ventricular zone and rhombic lip.
source: Different types of GABAergic and glutamatergic cerebellar neurons originate in temporal order from two progenitor niches, the ventricular zone and rhombic lip, which express the transcription factors Ptf1a and Atoh1, respectively.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge in cerebellar development and is referenced throughout the manuscript.

claim: The ventricular zone expresses the transcription factor Ptf1a.
source: Different types of GABAergic and glutamatergic cerebellar neurons originate in temporal order from two progenitor niches, the ventricular zone and rhombic lip, which express the transcription factors Ptf1a and Atoh1, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and confirmed by immunofluorescence data shown in the figures.

claim: The rhombic lip expresses the transcription factor Atoh1.
source: Different types of GABAergic and glutamatergic cerebellar neurons originate in temporal order from two progenitor niches, the ventricular zone and rhombic lip, which express the transcription factors Ptf1a and Atoh1, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge and confirmed by immunofluorescence data shown in the figures.

claim: Olig3 is a major determinant in generating the earliest neuronal derivatives emanating from both progenitor zones in mice.
source: Here, we uncover the transcription factor Olig3 as a major determinant in generating the earliest neuronal derivatives emanating from both progenitor zones in mice.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by lineage tracing experiments and mutant analysis presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: In the rhombic lip, Olig3 regulates progenitor cell proliferation.
source: In the rhombic lip, Olig3 regulates progenitor cell proliferation.
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation experiments showing reduced proliferation in Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).

claim: In the ventricular zone, Olig3 safeguards Purkinje cell specification by curtailing the expression of Pax2.
source: In the ventricular zone, Olig3 safeguards Purkinje cell specification by curtailing the expression of Pax2, a transcription factor that suppresses the Purkinje cell differentiation program.
evidence: This is supported by data showing ectopic Pax2 expression in Olig3 mutants (Figure 4) and overexpression experiments (Figure 5).

claim: Pax2 is a transcription factor that suppresses the Purkinje cell differentiation program.
source: In the ventricular zone, Olig3 safeguards Purkinje cell specification by curtailing the expression of Pax2, a transcription factor that suppresses the Purkinje cell differentiation program.
evidence: This is supported by overexpression experiments showing that Pax2 suppresses Foxp2 expression (Figure 5B).

claim: The cerebellum develops from the dorsal aspect of rhombomere 1 in mice at embryonic day 9.5.
source: The cerebellum develops from the dorsal aspect of rhombomere 1, a region known as the cerebellar anlage that in mice becomes apparent at embryonic (E) day 9.5 (Butts et al., 2014; Chizhikov et al., 2006; Millet et al., 1996; Morales and Hatten, 2006; Wingate and Hatten, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The cerebellar anlage contains two distinct germinal zones: the rhombic lip and the ventricular zone.
source: This region contains two distinct germinal zones, the rhombic lip and the ventricular zone, that generate all glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neurons, respectively (Alder et al., 1996; Hallonet et al., 1990; Wingate and Hatten, 1999; Zervas et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The rhombic lip generates all glutamatergic cerebellar neurons.
source: This region contains two distinct germinal zones, the rhombic lip and the ventricular zone, that generate all glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neurons, respectively (Alder et al., 1996; Hallonet et al., 1990; Wingate and Hatten, 1999; Zervas et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The ventricular zone generates all GABAergic cerebellar neurons.
source: This region contains two distinct germinal zones, the rhombic lip and the ventricular zone, that generate all glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neurons, respectively (Alder et al., 1996; Hallonet et al., 1990; Wingate and Hatten, 1999; Zervas et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Development of glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neurons largely depends on the differential expression of Atoh1 and Ptf1a.
source: Development of glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neurons largely depends on the differential expression of two basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) transcription factors: Atonal homolog one transcription factor (Atoh1) and Pancreas-specific transcription factor 1a (Ptf1a) (Gazit et al., 2004; Hoshino et al., 2005; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Millen et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2005; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of deep cerebellar nuclei neurons between E10.5 and E13.5.
source: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of three neuronal derivatives: (i) deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neurons (between E10.5 and E13.5), (ii) external granule layer (EGL) cells (between E13.5 and birth), which are the precursors of the internal granule layer cells that develop during early postnatal life, and (iii) unipolar brush cells (between E15.5 and the first days of postnatal life) (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Englund et al., 2006; Fink, 2006; Gazit et al., 2004; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Machold et al., 2011; Sekerková et al., 2004; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of external granule layer cells between E13.5 and birth.
source: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of three neuronal derivatives: (i) deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neurons (between E10.5 and E13.5), (ii) external granule layer (EGL) cells (between E13.5 and birth), which are the precursors of the internal granule layer cells that develop during early postnatal life, and (iii) unipolar brush cells (between E15.5 and the first days of postnatal life) (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Englund et al., 2006; Fink, 2006; Gazit et al., 2004; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Machold et al., 2011; Sekerková et al., 2004; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: External granule layer cells are the precursors of the internal granule layer cells that develop during early postnatal life.
source: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of three neuronal derivatives: (i) deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neurons (between E10.5 and E13.5), (ii) external granule layer (EGL) cells (between E13.5 and birth), which are the precursors of the internal granule layer cells that develop during early postnatal life, and (iii) unipolar brush cells (between E15.5 and the first days of postnatal life) (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Englund et al., 2006; Fink, 2006; Gazit et al., 2004; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Machold et al., 2011; Sekerková et al., 2004; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of unipolar brush cells between E15.5 and the first days of postnatal life.
source: In the rhombic lip, Atoh1 directs the generation of three neuronal derivatives: (i) deep cerebellar nuclei (DCN) neurons (between E10.5 and E13.5), (ii) external granule layer (EGL) cells (between E13.5 and birth), which are the precursors of the internal granule layer cells that develop during early postnatal life, and (iii) unipolar brush cells (between E15.5 and the first days of postnatal life) (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Englund et al., 2006; Fink, 2006; Gazit et al., 2004; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Machold et al., 2011; Sekerková et al., 2004; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: In the ventricular zone, Ptf1a instructs the generation of Purkinje cells between E11.5-E13.5.
source: In the ventricular zone, Ptf1a instructs the generation of Purkinje cells (between E11.5-E13.5) and all inhibitory interneurons, including Golgi, Stellate, and Basket cells (between E14.5 and birth).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field and confirmed by data in the manuscript.

claim: In the ventricular zone, Ptf1a instructs the generation of all inhibitory interneurons, including Golgi, Stellate, and Basket cells between E14.5 and birth.
source: In the ventricular zone, Ptf1a instructs the generation of Purkinje cells (between E11.5-E13.5) and all inhibitory interneurons, including Golgi, Stellate, and Basket cells (between E14.5 and birth).
evidence: This is supported by established knowledge in the field.

claim: Inhibitory interneurons are characterized by the expression of the homeodomain transcription factor Pax2.
source: Inhibitory interneurons are characterized by the expression of the homeodomain transcription factor Pax2 (Hashimoto and Mikoshiba, 2003; Hoshino et al., 2005; Leto et al., 2006; Maricich and Herrup, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Ablation of Atoh1 severely impairs glutamatergic cerebellar neuron development.
source: Although the ablation of Atoh1 and Ptf1a severely impairs glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neuron development (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Hoshino et al., 2005; Jensen, 2004; Sellick et al., 2004), less is known about the molecular machinery required for the temporal specification of the different neuronal derivatives emerging from the two cerebellar neurogenic niches.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ablation of Ptf1a severely impairs GABAergic cerebellar neuron development.
source: Although the ablation of Atoh1 and Ptf1a severely impairs glutamatergic and GABAergic cerebellar neuron development (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Hoshino et al., 2005; Jensen, 2004; Sellick et al., 2004), less is known about the molecular machinery required for the temporal specification of the different neuronal derivatives emerging from the two cerebellar neurogenic niches.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: bHLH transcription factors are master regulators of progenitor cell differentiation during development.
source: bHLH transcription factors are master regulators of progenitor cell differentiation during development and are critical players in neuron subtype specification in the nervous system (Atchley and Fitch, 1997; Baker and Brown, 2018; Ben-Arie et al., 2000; Bertrand et al., 2002; Dennis et al., 2019; Dokucu et al., 1996; Imayoshi and Kageyama, 2014; Jones, 2004; Mattar et al., 2008; Ross et al., 2003; Sommer et al., 1996).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Olig3 has been implicated in the specification of dorsally emerging neuron types in the hindbrain and spinal cord.
source: Among these factors, Oligodendrocyte factor 3 (Olig3) has been implicated in the specification of dorsally emerging neuron types in the hindbrain and spinal cord (Hernandez-Miranda et al., 2017b; Liu et al., 2008; Müller et al., 2005; Storm et al., 2009; Zechner et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Olig3 expression was previously reported during cerebellar development.
source: Although Olig3 expression was previously reported during cerebellar development, its function there has not yet been explored (Liu et al., 2010; Takebayashi et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The function of Olig3 in cerebellar development has not yet been explored.
source: Although Olig3 expression was previously reported during cerebellar development, its function there has not yet been explored (Liu et al., 2010; Takebayashi et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by the lack of prior functional studies cited.

claim: 51 bHLH genes were expressed during cerebellar development.
source: We found that 51 bHLH genes were expressed during cerebellar development, of which 27 were seen in progenitor niches (rhombic lip, ventricular zone, and/or EGL), and the remainder in postmitotic regions (Figure 1A; Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas data presented in Figure 1A and Table 1.

claim: 27 bHLH genes were seen in progenitor niches (rhombic lip, ventricular zone, and/or EGL).
source: We found that 51 bHLH genes were expressed during cerebellar development, of which 27 were seen in progenitor niches (rhombic lip, ventricular zone, and/or EGL), and the remainder in postmitotic regions (Figure 1A; Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas data presented in Figure 1A and Table 1.

claim: 9 bHLH genes displayed differential spatial-temporal expression patterns in the rhombic lip, EGL, and ventricular zone.
source: In particular, 9/27 genes displayed differential spatial-temporal expression patterns in the rhombic lip (Atoh1 and Olig3 between E11.5-E13.5), EGL (Atoh1 and Neurod1 between E13.5-birth), and ventricular zone (Ptf1a, Ascl1, Olig3, and Olig2 between E11.5-E13.5; Ptf1a, Neurod6, Neurog1 and Neurog2 between E13.5-E18.5).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas data.

claim: Atoh1 and Olig3 are expressed in the rhombic lip between E11.5-E13.5.
source: In particular, 9/27 genes displayed differential spatial-temporal expression patterns in the rhombic lip (Atoh1 and Olig3 between E11.5-E13.5), EGL (Atoh1 and Neurod1 between E13.5-birth), and ventricular zone (Ptf1a, Ascl1, Olig3, and Olig2 between E11.5-E13.5; Ptf1a, Neurod6, Neurog1 and Neurog2 between E13.5-E18.5).
evidence: This is supported by analysis of the Allen Developing Mouse Brain Atlas data and confirmed by immunofluorescence in Figure 1.

claim: Olig3+ cells were abundant in the rhombic lip from E10.5 to E12.5.
source: In the rhombic lip, Olig3+ cells were abundant from E10.5 to E12.5, but their numbers declined by E13.5 and were rare by E14.5 (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Olig3+ cell numbers in the rhombic lip declined by E13.5 and were rare by E14.5.
source: In the rhombic lip, Olig3+ cells were abundant from E10.5 to E12.5, but their numbers declined by E13.5 and were rare by E14.5 (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Almost all (>98%) Olig3+ rhombic lip cells co-expressed the progenitor marker Sox2 between E10.5 and E12.5.
source: Almost all (>98%) Olig3+ rhombic lip cells co-expressed the progenitor marker Sox2 between E10.5 and E12.5, but this co-localization, as well as the total number of Olig3+ cells, declined by E13.5 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: About 95% of proliferative BrdU+ cells in the rhombic lip co-expressed Olig3.
source: In addition, most (>95%) proliferative BrdU+ cells in the rhombic lip co-expressed Olig3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C.

claim: About 30% of Olig3+ cells in the rhombic lip expressed Atoh1.
source: Lastly, about 30% of Olig3+ cells in the rhombic lip expressed Atoh1 (Olig3+/Atoh1+ cells; Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In the rhombic lip, Olig3+ cells are progenitors, and a third of them co-express Atoh1.
source: Thus, in the rhombic lip, Olig3+ cells are progenitors, and a third of them co-express Atoh1.
evidence: This is an inference based on the data showing Sox2 and Atoh1 co-expression with Olig3.

claim: Olig3+ cells were first seen in the ventricular zone at E11.5.
source: In the ventricular zone, Olig3+ cells were first seen at E11.5. Their numbers peaked by E12.5 and became rare by E14.5 (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Olig3+ cell numbers in the ventricular zone peaked by E12.5 and became rare by E14.5.
source: In the ventricular zone, Olig3+ cells were first seen at E11.5. Their numbers peaked by E12.5 and became rare by E14.5 (Figure 1B; Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: Most Olig3+ cells (59%) in the ventricular zone co-expressed the progenitor marker Sox2 at E11.5 and E12.5.
source: Most Olig3+ cells (59%) in the ventricular zone co-expressed the progenitor marker Sox2 at E11.5 and E12.5, but this co-localization, as well as the total number of Olig3+ cells, declined by E13.5 (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: About one-third of the BrdU+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Olig3.
source: Furthermore, about one-third of the BrdU+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Olig3 (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2D.

claim: 52% of the Olig3+ ventricular zone cells co-expressed Ptf1a.
source: Lastly, 52% of the Olig3+ ventricular zone cells co-expressed Ptf1a, while 41% co-expressed the postmitotic Purkinje cell marker Foxp2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 41% of Olig3+ ventricular zone cells co-expressed the postmitotic Purkinje cell marker Foxp2.
source: Lastly, 52% of the Olig3+ ventricular zone cells co-expressed Ptf1a, while 41% co-expressed the postmitotic Purkinje cell marker Foxp2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Most Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone are progenitors (Olig3+/Ptf1a+/Foxp2-).
source: This indicates that whereas most Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone are progenitors (Olig3+/Ptf1a+/Foxp2-), Olig3 is transiently retained in early-born Purkinje cells (Olig3+/Ptf1a-/Foxp2+).
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Olig3 is transiently retained in early-born Purkinje cells (Olig3+/Ptf1a-/Foxp2+).
source: This indicates that whereas most Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone are progenitors (Olig3+/Ptf1a+/Foxp2-), Olig3 is transiently retained in early-born Purkinje cells (Olig3+/Ptf1a-/Foxp2+).
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Olig3 is expressed in rhombic lip and ventricular zone progenitor cells during the generation of their earliest neuronal derivatives.
source: We conclude that Olig3 is expressed in rhombic lip and ventricular zone progenitor cells during the generation of their earliest neuronal derivatives.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the temporal expression data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Tomato+ cells were broadly distributed across the entire cerebellum of Olig3creERT2/+; Rosa26lsl-tdT/+ mice recombined at E10.5 and analyzed at E19.
source: Three-dimensional reconstructions of recombined brains showed that Tomato+ cells were broadly distributed across the entire cerebellum of Olig3creERT2/+; Rosa26lsl-tdT/+ mice (Figure 2A–B; Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–A'').
evidence: This is supported by lightsheet microscopy data shown in Figure 2A-B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A-A''.

claim: Tomato+ cells were observed in the EGL, Purkinje cell layer, and dense groups encompassing the three DCN nuclei in Olig3creERT2/+; Rosa26lsl-tdT/+ mice.
source: In particular, we observed Tomato+ cells in the EGL, Purkinje cell layer, and dense groups of Tomato+ cells encompassing the three nuclei formed by DCN neurons: the nucleus dentatus, interpositus, and fastigii (Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by lightsheet microscopy data shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Tomato+ cells co-expressed Tbr1 (a marker of Fastigii DCN cells) and Brn2 (a marker of Interpositus and Dentatus DCN cells).
source: Closer inspection revealed that Tomato+ cells co-expressed Tbr1 (a marker of Fastigii DCN cells) and Brn2 (a marker of Interpositus and Dentatus DCN cells; Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Most EGL and DCN cells have a history of Olig3 expression.
source: Our long-term lineage-tracing studies demonstrated that most EGL and DCN cells have a history of Olig3 expression, ablation of which massively reduced their cell numbers.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The majority (62%) of Pax6+ postmitotic cells, outside the EGL, co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5.
source: We observed that the majority (62%) of Pax6+ postmitotic cells, outside the EGL, co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5, but the proportion of Pax6+/βgal+ cells dropped when recombination was induced at later stages (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Most Tbr1+ (>99%) DCN neurons co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5.
source: Furthermore, we found that most Tbr1+ (>99%) DCN neurons, Foxp2+ (51%) Purkinje cells, and Brn2+ (43%) DCN neurons co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5, but the proportion of double-positive cells declined when recombination was induced at later stages (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2F.

claim: 51% of Foxp2+ Purkinje cells co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5.
source: Furthermore, we found that most Tbr1+ (>99%) DCN neurons, Foxp2+ (51%) Purkinje cells, and Brn2+ (43%) DCN neurons co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5 or E11.5, but the proportion of double-positive cells declined when recombination was induced at later stages (Figure 2F,G; Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Few Pax2+ (6%) cells co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5.
source: In contrast, few Pax2+ (6%) cells co-expressed βgal when recombination was induced at E10.5, and the number of double-positive cells was minimal when recombination was induced at later stages (Figure 2H).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 2H.

claim: Olig3+ progenitor cells substantially contribute to the generation of the earliest derivatives of the ventricular zone (Purkinje cells) and rhombic lip (DCN neurons).
source: We conclude that Olig3+ progenitor cells substantially contribute to the generation of the earliest derivatives of the ventricular zone (Purkinje cells) and rhombic lip (DCN neurons), and partially contribute to the later arising EGL cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing data presented in Figure 2.

claim: At birth (P0), the cerebella of Olig3 null mutant mice were drastically reduced in volume when compared to control littermates.
source: At birth (P0), the cerebella of Olig3 null (Olig3-/-) mutant mice were drastically reduced in volume when compared to control (Olig3+/-) littermates (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by volumetric analysis shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: The strongest reduction in volume was observed in the medial portion of the cerebella of Olig3 mutant mice.
source: The strongest reduction in volume was observed in the medial portion of the cerebella of Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by volumetric analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Olig3 mutant cerebella had less folia than control littermates.
source: Closer inspection of Olig3 mutant cerebella revealed that they had less folia than control littermates (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Ablation of Olig3 results in severe cerebellar hypoplasia.
source: Thus, ablation of Olig3 results in severe cerebellar hypoplasia.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the volumetric and histological data presented in Figure 3.

claim: The number of Tbr1+, Brn2+, Pax6+, and Foxp2+ neurons was greatly reduced in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Furthermore, the number of Tbr1+, Brn2+, Pax6+, and Foxp2+ neurons was greatly reduced in Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 3C–E; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3C-E and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The number of Pax2+ inhibitory interneurons increased in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: In contrast, the number of Pax2+ inhibitory interneurons increased in mutant mice (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Late born derivatives from the rhombic lip, such as Tbr2+ unipolar brush cells, were correctly specified in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Late born derivatives from the rhombic lip, such as Tbr2+ unipolar brush cells, were correctly specified in Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Olig3 is critically involved in cerebellar development and the generation of DCN neurons, EGL cells (including their granule cell derivatives) and Purkinje cells.
source: Together these data show that Olig3 is critically involved in cerebellar development and the generation of DCN neurons, EGL cells (including their granule cell derivatives) and Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant phenotype data presented in Figure 3.

claim: E13.5 Olig3 mutant mice showed a severe reduction in the number of DCN and EGL cells.
source: Compared to control littermates, E13.5 Olig3 mutant mice showed a severe reduction in the number of DCN and EGL cells but no significant reduction in the number of Purkinje cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: E13.5 Olig3 mutant mice showed no significant reduction in the number of Purkinje cells.
source: Compared to control littermates, E13.5 Olig3 mutant mice showed a severe reduction in the number of DCN and EGL cells but no significant reduction in the number of Purkinje cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The deficits observed in DCN neurons and EGL cells arise early during cerebellar development in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Therefore, while the deficits observed in DCN neurons and EGL cells arise early during cerebellar development in Olig3 mutant mice, the reduction in Purkinje cell numbers occurs at a later developmental stage than E13.5 (see below).
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal analysis of the mutant phenotype.

claim: The reduction in Purkinje cell numbers in Olig3 mutant mice occurs at a later developmental stage than E13.5.
source: Therefore, while the deficits observed in DCN neurons and EGL cells arise early during cerebellar development in Olig3 mutant mice, the reduction in Purkinje cell numbers occurs at a later developmental stage than E13.5 (see below).
evidence: This is an inference based on the temporal analysis of the mutant phenotype.

claim: Analysis of Olig3 mutant mice at E11.5 and E12.5 revealed reduced numbers of Atoh1+ cells in the rhombic lip.
source: Analysis of Olig3 mutant mice at E11.5 and E12.5 revealed reduced numbers of Atoh1+ cells in the rhombic lip, but no change in the number of Ptf1a+ cells in the ventricular zone (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A.

claim: Analysis of Olig3 mutant mice at E11.5 and E12.5 revealed no change in the number of Ptf1a+ cells in the ventricular zone.
source: Analysis of Olig3 mutant mice at E11.5 and E12.5 revealed reduced numbers of Atoh1+ cells in the rhombic lip, but no change in the number of Ptf1a+ cells in the ventricular zone (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3B.

claim: In the rhombic lip, the number of proliferative (BrdU+) cells was reduced in Olig3 mutant animals.
source: In the rhombic lip, the number of proliferative (BrdU+) cells was reduced in Olig3 mutant animals (Figure 3—figure supplement 3C).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU incorporation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3C.

claim: No change in the number of Tunel+ apoptotic bodies were seen in the rhombic lip of Olig3 mutant animals at any of the analyzed embryonic stages.
source: However, no change in the number of Tunel+ apoptotic bodies (puncta) were seen at any of the analyzed embryonic stages (Figure 3—figure supplement 3E).
evidence: This is supported by Tunel assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3E.

claim: In the ventricular zone of Olig3 mutant animals neither the number of BrdU+ or Tunel+ apoptotic bodies changed.
source: In the ventricular zone of Olig3 mutant animals neither the number of BrdU+ or Tunel+ apoptotic bodies changed (Figure 3—figure supplement 3D,E).
evidence: This is supported by BrdU and Tunel assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3D,E.

claim: The mutation of Olig3 impairs progenitor proliferation in the rhombic lip but not in the ventricular zone.
source: Thus, the mutation of Olig3 impairs progenitor proliferation in the rhombic lip but not in the ventricular zone, illustrating that Olig3's function in the ventricular zone differs from that in the rhombic lip.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the proliferation and apoptosis data.

claim: Olig3's function in the ventricular zone differs from that in the rhombic lip.
source: Thus, the mutation of Olig3 impairs progenitor proliferation in the rhombic lip but not in the ventricular zone, illustrating that Olig3's function in the ventricular zone differs from that in the rhombic lip.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential effects of Olig3 mutation in the two progenitor zones.

claim: In wildtype and heterozygous Olig3GFP/+ mice, Pax2+ cells first appeared at E13.5 in a rostral domain of the ventricular zone that lacked expression of Olig3.
source: In wildtype and heterozygous Olig3GFP/+ mice, Pax2+ cells first appeared at E13.5 in a rostral domain of the ventricular zone that lacked expression of Olig3, and by E14.5 occupied most of the ventricular zone (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: By E14.5, Pax2+ cells occupied most of the ventricular zone in wildtype and heterozygous Olig3GFP/+ mice.
source: In wildtype and heterozygous Olig3GFP/+ mice, Pax2+ cells first appeared at E13.5 in a rostral domain of the ventricular zone that lacked expression of Olig3, and by E14.5 occupied most of the ventricular zone (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The spread of Pax2+ cells from rostral to caudal coincided with the receding of Olig3+ cells.
source: The spread of Pax2+ cells from rostral to caudal coincided with the receding of Olig3+ cells (schematically displayed in Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an observation based on the temporal and spatial expression patterns shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Supernumerary Pax2+ cells were found in Olig3GFP/GFP mutant mice from E13.5 to P0.
source: In sharp contrast to wildtype and heterozygous Olig3GFP/+ mice, we found supernumerary Pax2+ cells in Olig3GFP/GFP mutant mice from E13.5 to P0 (Figure 4C; Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2; quantified in Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: Many of the supernumerary Pax2+ cells co-expressed GFP at E13.5 and E14.5 in Olig3GFP/GFP mutant mice.
source: Many of the supernumerary Pax2+ cells co-expressed GFP at E13.5 and E14.5 (see magnifications in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The ablation of Olig3 de-represses Pax2 in the early developing cerebellum.
source: Thus, the ablation of Olig3 de-represses Pax2 in the early developing cerebellum.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the ectopic Pax2 expression observed in Olig3 mutants.

claim: At E13.5, most Foxp2+ cells (52%) co-expressed Pax2 in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Surprisingly at E13.5, most Foxp2+ cells (52%) co-expressed Pax2 in Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 4C, quantified in Figure 4E), vice versa, roughly 90% of the Pax2+ cells co-expressed Foxp2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 4C,E.

claim: At E13.5, roughly 90% of the Pax2+ cells co-expressed Foxp2 in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Surprisingly at E13.5, most Foxp2+ cells (52%) co-expressed Pax2 in Olig3 mutant mice (Figure 4C, quantified in Figure 4E), vice versa, roughly 90% of the Pax2+ cells co-expressed Foxp2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The proportion of misspecified Foxp2+/Pax2+ cells declined by E14.5 and became rare by P0 in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: Interestingly, the proportion of misspecified Foxp2+/Pax2+ (or Pax2+/Foxp2+) cells declined by E14.5 and became rare by P0 (quantified in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 4E and Figure 4—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The decrease of misspecified (Foxp2+/Pax2+) cells coincided with the increase of inhibitory (Foxp2-/Pax2+) interneurons seen in Olig3 mutant animals.
source: The decrease of misspecified (Foxp2+/Pax2+) cells coincided with the increase of inhibitory (Foxp2-/Pax2+) interneurons seen in Olig3 mutant animals (compare Figure 4D and Figure 4E).
evidence: This is an observation based on comparing the quantifications in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: Misspecified (Foxp2+/Pax2+) cells in Olig3 mutant animals undergo a fate shift and adopt an inhibitory (Foxp2-/Pax2+) interneuron identity.
source: We thus hypothesized that misspecified (Foxp2+/Pax2+) cells in Olig3 mutant animals might undergo a fate shift and adopt an inhibitory (Foxp2-/Pax2+) interneuron identity.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the temporal correlation between the decrease in misspecified cells and increase in interneurons, which is tested by lineage tracing.

claim: There was an increase in the proportion of Pax2+/βgal+ cells in Olig3creERT2/GFP;MaptnLacZ/+ mice when compared to Olig3creERT2/+;MaptnLacZ/+ control littermates.
source: We found an increase in the proportion of Pax2+/βgal+ cells in Olig3creERT2/GFP;MaptnLacZ/+ mice when compared to Olig3creERT2/+;MaptnLacZ/+ control littermates (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Ectopic Pax2+/βgal+ cells in Olig3creERT2/GFP;MaptnLacZ/+ mice adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity and intermingle with Pax2+/βgal- cells underneath the Purkinje cell layer at E19.
source: Notably, ectopic Pax2+/βgal+ cells in Olig3creERT2/GFP;MaptnLacZ/+ mice not only adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity (Pax2 expression), but also intermingle with Pax2+/βgal- cells underneath the Purkinje cell layer at E19 (compare inserts 1 and 2 in Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Ablation of Olig3 in the ventricular zone results in the misspecification of Purkinje cells that later change their fate and adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity.
source: Taken together, we conclude that ablation of Olig3 in the ventricular zone results in the misspecification of Purkinje cells. These cells later change their fate and adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity (schematically displayed in Figure 4G).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing and temporal analysis data presented in Figure 4.

claim: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, no GFP+/Pax2+ cell co-expressed Foxp2.
source: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, no GFP+/Pax2+ cell co-expressed Foxp2, whereas in pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 72% of the GFP+ cells were also Foxp2+ (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 72% of the GFP+ cells were also Foxp2+.
source: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, no GFP+/Pax2+ cell co-expressed Foxp2, whereas in pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 72% of the GFP+ cells were also Foxp2+ (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Parvalbumin expression coincides with the onset of cerebellar interneuron specification and is virtually absent in Foxp2+ cells at E14.5.
source: Calcium-binding proteins are characteristic of inhibitory interneurons in the central nervous system, among which we found Parvalbumin expression to coincide with the onset of cerebellar interneuron specification and to be virtually absent in Foxp2+ cells at E14.5 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, a third of the Parvalbumin+ cells co-expressed GFP.
source: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, a third of the Parvalbumin+ cells co-expressed GFP, whereas in pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 4% of the GFP+ cells were also Parvalbumin+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 4% of the GFP+ cells were also Parvalbumin+.
source: In pCAG-Pax2-ires-GFP electroporated mice, a third of the Parvalbumin+ cells co-expressed GFP, whereas in pCAG-GFP + Empty-IRES-GFP electroporated mice about 4% of the GFP+ cells were also Parvalbumin+ (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pax2 is an efficient suppressor of Foxp2 expression.
source: We conclude that Pax2 is an efficient suppressor of Foxp2 expression and that its expression seems to induce a differentiation program characteristic of inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Pax2 expression seems to induce a differentiation program characteristic of inhibitory interneurons.
source: We conclude that Pax2 is an efficient suppressor of Foxp2 expression and that its expression seems to induce a differentiation program characteristic of inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overexpression experiments showing Parvalbumin induction.

claim: The proportion of GFP+ cells that co-expressed Pax2 was greatly reduced in the ventricular zone of Olig3-overexpressing embryos when compared to control electroporated mice.
source: The proportion of GFP+ cells that co-expressed Pax2 was greatly reduced in the ventricular zone of Olig3-overexpressing embryos when compared to control electroporated mice (Figure 5C, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by in utero electroporation data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Expression of Olig3 is sufficient to cell-autonomously suppress Pax2 expression.
source: Thus, expression of Olig3 is sufficient to cell-autonomously suppress Pax2 expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the Olig3 overexpression experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: During early development, Olig3 in the ventricular zone suppresses Pax2 in newborn Purkinje cells to prevent their misspecification and secure their identity.
source: We conclude that during early development, Olig3 in the ventricular zone suppresses Pax2 in newborn Purkinje cells to prevent their misspecification and secure their identity.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data from mutant analysis and overexpression experiments.

claim: Ablation of Ascl1 does not interfere with Purkinje cell development.
source: While ablation of Ascl1 does not interfere with Purkinje cell development (Grimaldi et al., 2009; Sudarov et al., 2011), the exact role of Olig2 in the generation of GABAergic derivatives is unclear (Ju et al., 2016; Seto et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Analysis of Olig2 null mutant mice found a reduction in Purkinje cell numbers and a modest increase in inhibitory interneurons.
source: In order to clarify the function of Olig2 we analyzed Olig2 null mutant mice and found a reduction in Purkinje cell numbers and a modest increase in inhibitory interneurons (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Roughly half of the Foxp2+ Purkinje cell population had a history of Olig2 expression.
source: This showed that while roughly half of the Foxp2+ Purkinje cell population had a history of Olig2 expression, few inhibitory interneurons were generated from Olig2+ progenitors (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Few inhibitory interneurons were generated from Olig2+ progenitors.
source: This showed that while roughly half of the Foxp2+ Purkinje cell population had a history of Olig2 expression, few inhibitory interneurons were generated from Olig2+ progenitors (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The phenotypes of Olig3 and Olig2 mutant mice partially overlap.
source: We thus conclude that the phenotypes of Olig3 and Olig2 mutant mice partially overlap (summarized in Figure 6A; Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparing the mutant phenotypes.

claim: Roughly 58% of Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Olig2 but not Foxp2.
source: We observed that roughly 58% of Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Olig2 but not Foxp2, while the remaining 42% of the Olig3+ cells co-expressed Foxp2 but not Olig2 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 42% of the Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Foxp2 but not Olig2.
source: We observed that roughly 58% of Olig3+ cells in the ventricular zone co-expressed Olig2 but not Foxp2, while the remaining 42% of the Olig3+ cells co-expressed Foxp2 but not Olig2 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence quantification shown in Figure 6B.

claim: No Olig3-/Olig2+ cells co-expressed Foxp2.
source: Notably, we observed no Olig3-/Olig2+ cells that co-expressed Foxp2, illustrating that differentiated Purkinje cells retain Olig3 but not Olig2 expression.
evidence: This is an observation based on the immunofluorescence data in Figure 6B.

claim: Differentiated Purkinje cells retain Olig3 but not Olig2 expression.
source: Notably, we observed no Olig3-/Olig2+ cells that co-expressed Foxp2, illustrating that differentiated Purkinje cells retain Olig3 but not Olig2 expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the co-expression patterns observed in Figure 6B.

claim: Mutation of Olig3 did not affect the expression of Olig2 in ventricular zone progenitors.
source: Mutation of Olig3 did not affect the expression of Olig2, and neither did mutation of Olig2 affect the expression of Olig3 in progenitor cells of the ventricular zone (Figure 6C and D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Mutation of Olig2 did not affect the expression of Olig3 in progenitor cells of the ventricular zone.
source: Mutation of Olig3 did not affect the expression of Olig2, and neither did mutation of Olig2 affect the expression of Olig3 in progenitor cells of the ventricular zone (Figure 6C and D; Figure 6—figure supplement 1E,F).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The expression of Olig3 and Olig2 in ventricular zone progenitor cells is independent of the other factor.
source: These data demonstrate that the expression of Olig3 and Olig2 in ventricular zone progenitor cells is independent of the other factor.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the cross-mutant analysis shown in Figure 6C,D.

claim: Numerous Foxp2+/Pax2+ misspecified cells were observed in Olig2 mutant animals at E13.5.
source: Indeed, we observed numerous Foxp2+/Pax2+ misspecified cells in Olig2 mutant animals at E13.5 (Figure 6E, quantified in Figure 6F), but unlike in Olig3 mutant embryos, these cells were only located in the rostral-most part of the ventricular zone (compare insets in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: In Olig2 mutant embryos, Foxp2+/Pax2+ misspecified cells were only located in the rostral-most part of the ventricular zone.
source: Indeed, we observed numerous Foxp2+/Pax2+ misspecified cells in Olig2 mutant animals at E13.5 (Figure 6E, quantified in Figure 6F), but unlike in Olig3 mutant embryos, these cells were only located in the rostral-most part of the ventricular zone (compare insets in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Olig2 specifically suppresses Pax2 in rostrally generated Purkinje cells.
source: These data demonstrate that Olig2 specifically suppresses Pax2 in rostrally generated Purkinje cells, while Olig3 has a broader function in the suppression of Pax2 in most of the Purkinje cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the spatial distribution of misspecified cells in Olig2 mutants.

claim: Olig3 has a broader function in the suppression of Pax2 in most of the Purkinje cell population.
source: These data demonstrate that Olig2 specifically suppresses Pax2 in rostrally generated Purkinje cells, while Olig3 has a broader function in the suppression of Pax2 in most of the Purkinje cell population.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparing the spatial distribution of misspecified cells in Olig2 and Olig3 mutants.

claim: Olig3 and Olig2 complementarily contribute to the correct specification of Purkinje cells by curtailing the expression of Pax2.
source: We therefore conclude that Olig3 and Olig2 complementarily contribute to the correct specification of Purkinje cells by curtailing the expression of Pax2 (schematically displayed in Figure 6G).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined analysis of Olig2 and Olig3 mutants.

claim: Ablation of Olig3 results in pronounced cerebellar hypoplasia at birth and the massive loss of DCN neurons, EGL cells including their granule cell derivatives, and Purkinje cells.
source: We report here that Olig3 is a key player in cerebellar development and the generation of its earliest neuronal derivatives. Ablation of Olig3 results in pronounced cerebellar hypoplasia at birth and the massive loss of DCN neurons, EGL cells including their granule cell derivatives, and Purkinje cells.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Olig3 regulates progenitor cell proliferation in the rhombic lip.
source: Our data illustrate that Olig3 regulates progenitor cell proliferation in the rhombic lip, whereas in the ventricular zone Olig3 cell-autonomously suppresses the development of inhibitory interneurons by curtailing the expression of Pax2.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the ventricular zone Olig3 cell-autonomously suppresses the development of inhibitory interneurons by curtailing the expression of Pax2.
source: Our data illustrate that Olig3 regulates progenitor cell proliferation in the rhombic lip, whereas in the ventricular zone Olig3 cell-autonomously suppresses the development of inhibitory interneurons by curtailing the expression of Pax2.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Pax2 acts as an effective suppressor of the Purkinje cells differentiation program.
source: We demonstrate that Pax2 acts as an effective suppressor of the Purkinje cells differentiation program.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by overexpression data in Figure 5.

claim: Olig3 and its close family member Olig2 specify complementary Purkinje cell populations.
source: In addition, we show that Olig3 and its close family member Olig2 specify complementary Purkinje cell populations.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Loss of Atoh1 results in the severe reduction of EGL cells and impairs the development of DCN neurons.
source: Earlier studies revealed that these rhombic lip derivatives depend on Atoh1 for their development, as loss of Atoh1 results in the severe reduction of EGL cells and impairs the development of DCN neurons (Ben-Arie et al., 1997; Gazit et al., 2004; Jensen, 2004; Machold and Fishell, 2005; Machold et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2005; Yamada et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Olig3 is essential for DCN neuron development.
source: This temporal window overlaps with the generation of DCN cells (Fink, 2006; Sekerková et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2005; Yamada et al., 2014), which are the most reduced neuron type in Olig3 mutant mice (this study). Thus, Olig3 is essential for DCN neuron development.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant phenotype and lineage tracing data.

claim: The severe loss of EGL cells and their granule cell derivatives seems to largely account for the pronounced cerebellar hypoplasia observed in Olig3 mutant mice.
source: The severe loss of EGL cells and their granule cell derivatives seems to largely account for the pronounced cerebellar hypoplasia observed in Olig3 mutant mice, and has also been observed after the loss of EGL cells in other studies (Ben-Arie et al., 1997).
evidence: This is an inference based on the mutant phenotype and comparison to other studies.

claim: The reduced numbers of granule cells in Olig3 mutant mice might be mainly independent of Olig3 and due to the reduction of instructive signals emanating from Purkinje cells.
source: One should note, however, that the reduced numbers of granule cells in Olig3 mutant mice might be mainly independent of Olig3 and due to the reduction of instructive signals emanating from Purkinje cells, which are severely affected in these mutant mice.
evidence: This is speculation based on known interactions between Purkinje cells and granule cells.

claim: Purkinje cells regulate EGL proliferation and the differentiation of granule cells via sonic hedgehog signaling.
source: Indeed, available evidence shows that Purkinje cells regulate EGL proliferation and the differentiation of granule cells via sonic hedgehog signaling (Dahmane and Ruiz i Altaba, 1999; Wallace, 1999; Wechsler-Reya and Scott, 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There exists a dorsal progenitor domain (called dA1) in rhombomeres 2–7 that co-expresses Olig3 and Atoh1.
source: During the development of rhombomeres 2–7, there exists a dorsal progenitor domain (called dA1) that also co-expresses Olig3 and Atoh1 (Hernandez-Miranda et al., 2017a; Liu et al., 2008; Storm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The dA1 domain generates the mossy fiber precerebellar (pontine, lateral reticular, external cuneate) nuclei.
source: During the development of rhombomeres 2–7, there exists a dorsal progenitor domain (called dA1) that also co-expresses Olig3 and Atoh1 (Hernandez-Miranda et al., 2017a; Liu et al., 2008; Storm et al., 2009). This domain generates the mossy fiber precerebellar (pontine, lateral reticular, external cuneate) nuclei.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ablation of Olig3 greatly reduces the number of Atoh1+ cells in the dA1 domain and their derivatives.
source: Like in the rhombic lip, ablation of Olig3 greatly reduces the number of Atoh1+ cells in this area and their derivatives (Liu et al., 2008; Storm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Ablation of Olig3 in the spinal cord reduces Atoh1+ progenitor cells.
source: This phenomenon also occurs in the spinal cord when Olig3 is ablated (Müller et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study.

claim: Olig3 has a conserved function in the proliferation of Atoh1+ progenitor cells.
source: Thus, Olig3 has a conserved function in the proliferation of Atoh1+ progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the consistent effects of Olig3 ablation across different CNS regions.

claim: The primary function of Olig3 in the ventricular zone is to secure the development of Purkinje cells by cell-autonomously suppressing an alternative program that specifies inhibitory interneurons.
source: Thus, the primary function of Olig3 in the ventricular zone is to secure the development of Purkinje cells by cell-autonomously suppressing an alternative program that specifies inhibitory interneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the mutant phenotype and overexpression data.

claim: Supernumerary inhibitory neurons become specified at the expense of excitatory neurons in the hindbrain and spinal cord of Olig3 mutant mice.
source: In agreement with our findings, it was previously shown that supernumerary inhibitory neurons become specified at the expense of excitatory neurons in the hindbrain and spinal cord of Olig3 mutant mice (Müller et al., 2005; Storm et al., 2009; Zechner et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: There is a unique progenitor domain in rhombomere 7 (called dA4) that co-expresses Olig3 and Ptf1a, which generates the pre-cerebellar climbing fiber neurons of the inferior olive.
source: Interestingly, there is a unique progenitor domain in rhombomere 7 (called dA4) that co-expresses Olig3 and Ptf1a, which generates the pre-cerebellar climbing fiber neurons of the inferior olive (reviewed in Hernandez-Miranda et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: In the absence of Olig3, inferior olive neurons and many spinal cord excitatory neurons seem to change their fate and erroneously adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity.
source: In the absence of Olig3, inferior olive neurons and many spinal cord excitatory neurons seem to change their fate and erroneously adopt an inhibitory interneuron identity (Liu et al., 2008; Müller et al., 2005; Storm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Inhibitory interneurons are the default neuronal type generated from the brainstem, spinal cord and the ventricular zone of the cerebellum.
source: This suggests that inhibitory interneurons are the default neuronal type generated from the brainstem, spinal cord and the ventricular zone of the cerebellum.
evidence: This is speculation based on the consistent fate changes observed in Olig3 mutants across different CNS regions.

claim: Seto et al., 2014 postulated a 'temporal identity transition' model in which Olig2+ Purkinje cell progenitors transition into inhibitory interneuron progenitors.
source: Based on short-term lineage-tracing experiments, Seto et al., 2014 postulated a 'temporal identity transition' model in which Olig2+ Purkinje cell progenitors transition into inhibitory interneuron progenitors (Seto et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a citation to a previous study.

claim: Long-term lineage-tracing experiments using Olig2cre and Olig3creERT2 mice showed that Pax2+ inhibitory interneurons rarely have a history of Olig2 or Olig3 expression.
source: In keeping with observations made by Ju et al., 2016, our long-term lineage-tracing experiments using Olig2cre and Olig3creERT2 mice showed that Pax2+ inhibitory interneurons rarely have a history of Olig2 or Olig3 expression.
evidence: This is supported by lineage tracing data in Figure 2H and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Neither Olig2 nor Olig3 control the transition of early (Purkinje) to late (inhibitory interneuron) ventricular zone progenitor cells.
source: Our data unambiguously show that neither Olig2 nor Olig3 control the transition of early (Purkinje) to late (inhibitory interneuron) ventricular zone progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lineage tracing data.

claim: Olig2 and Olig3 are essential for the correct specification of Purkinje cells by curtailing an inhibitory interneuron transcriptional program.
source: Rather, our work demonstrates that these factors are essential for the correct specification of Purkinje cells by curtailing an inhibitory interneuron transcriptional program.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined mutant and overexpression data.

claim: Cerebellar DCN neurons and internal granule cells develop from Olig3+/Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitor cells.
source: Here, we show that cerebellar DCN neurons and internal granule cells develop from Olig3+/Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitor cells, whereas Purkinje cells derive from Olig3+/Ptf1a+ ventricular zone progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by lineage tracing data.

claim: Purkinje cells derive from Olig3+/Ptf1a+ ventricular zone progenitors.
source: Here, we show that cerebellar DCN neurons and internal granule cells develop from Olig3+/Atoh1+ rhombic lip progenitor cells, whereas Purkinje cells derive from Olig3+/Ptf1a+ ventricular zone progenitors.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings supported by lineage tracing data.

claim: In the mature cerebellum, DCN neurons and granule cells receive input from brainstem precerebellar mossy fiber neurons that originate from progenitor cells that co-express Olig3 and Atoh1.
source: In the mature cerebellum, DCN neurons and granule cells receive input from brainstem precerebellar mossy fiber neurons that originate from progenitor cells that co-express Olig3 and Atoh1, whilst Purkinje cells receive input from climbing fiber neurons that emerge from progenitors that co-express Olig3 and Ptf1a (Liu et al., 2008; Storm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and represents established knowledge about cerebellar circuitry.

claim: Purkinje cells receive input from climbing fiber neurons that emerge from progenitors that co-express Olig3 and Ptf1a.
source: In the mature cerebellum, DCN neurons and granule cells receive input from brainstem precerebellar mossy fiber neurons that originate from progenitor cells that co-express Olig3 and Atoh1, whilst Purkinje cells receive input from climbing fiber neurons that emerge from progenitors that co-express Olig3 and Ptf1a (Liu et al., 2008; Storm et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and represents established knowledge about cerebellar circuitry.
